rationale: bugs_open/092: page-content-writer's prepare_link_context step builds the 'only link to these pages' block for the writer prompt, and it has been fed nothing since at least 2026-03-28. It looks for its page list only in collected_data, at a configured field (db_sync.pages) plus three fallbacks (site_plan.pages, pages_to_build.pages, render_context.available_pages). None of the four has ever existed on that orchestration. Measured live 2026-07-31: 26 of 26 page-content-writer runs recorded page_count 0 and an empty link_constraint_text, latest 15:36 UTC today. The same gap is recorded as concept-register LNK-017, filed 2026-06-12 with status 'partial' and naming these same two candidate fixes, so this is a seven-week-old known defect, not a fresh discovery. The consequence is not cosmetic: the consuming prompt template guards the block with {{if .link_context.link_constraint_text}}, so an empty string removes the entire '## Internal Linking' section and the model writes internal links with no idea what pages exist. Of the 15 unique phantom targets the deploy gate caught in its retained window, 15 were pure inventions. The downstream mitigation that used to absorb this (bugs_open/079's RepairPageLinks) was proven on 2026-07-28 to have its output discarded at persistence, so there is currently no backstop at all and these links reach live pages as 404s. Fix candidate 2 (populate db_sync.pages on this path) was ruled out on 2026-07-27 by the bug's filer -- there is no array of pages anywhere on that orchestration to point the field at -- and re-confirmed from the other side today: of 26 writer orchestrations, db_sync is present on 0, site_record on 0, top-level site_id on 0, and input_data.site_id on 26. So candidate 1, have the action read the database itself, is the only option, and this is a Go change plus a chassis roll rather than a config tweak. Intent: make the writer's allow-list the SAME SET the deploy gate validates against, and make an empty list say so explicitly instead of silently emitting nothing.

plan.summary: prepare_link_context now reads the site's real pages from the database, under exactly the predicate validate_page_content's loadValidPagePaths uses to decide what is a phantom_link, so the writer's allow-list and the gate's accept-set are the same set by construction. collected_data remains the fallback. An empty page list now emits an explicit 'do not create any internal links' instruction instead of the empty string that made the consuming template drop the whole prompt section. The two causes of an empty list -- 'the site has no pages' and 'I could not find out' -- are now distinguished in the output (degraded, db_consulted, reason) and the second writes a durable agent_error_log row. URL synthesis from a page name is removed. The dead duplicate link_constraints.go is deleted.

edits.rationale: The authoritative read that the action never had. The predicate is copied verbatim from validate_page_content.go's loadValidPagePaths because THAT function decides what the deploy gate calls a phantom_link -- if the writer is constrained from any other source the two can disagree, and a writer obeying its own instructions gets its links flagged. Measured 2026-07-31 the fleet has exactly two page statuses (active 449, archived 23), so this predicate and maintenance_actions.go's status='active' are extensionally identical today; the gate's is used because the invariant is about agreeing with the gate, not about being strict. An error is returned rather than an empty slice: a truncated allow-list would quietly forbid links to pages that exist, which is harder to notice than having no list at all (the same reasoning loadValidPagePaths records for its trustworthy bool).

Wires the database as the primary source with collected_data as the fallback, and separates 'the site has no pages' from 'I could not find out'. Those two states had the same observable (empty list + logger.Warn) and have opposite remedies, which is a large part of why this ran at 100% failure for seven weeks unnoticed. degraded is deliberately NOT 'the list is empty' -- it is 'the list could not be ESTABLISHED' -- so a brand-new site with no pages does not read as a broken run. The explicit config opt-out (enabled:false) still returns an empty string, because that is the one case where saying nothing is correct.

This is the actual fail-open. Returning "" for an empty list meant the one input where guidance matters most produced NO guidance at all, and the consuming template's {{if}} guard then removed even the heading -- so a writer that knew nothing about the site was told nothing and invented destinations. An empty list now states that explicitly, which is true in both states that produce it and is the safest available instruction. Also drops the text's own '## Internal Links' heading: the live page-content-writer template emits '## Internal Linking' on the line immediately above this interpolation, so the old heading rendered a duplicate.

The whole fix turns on finding a site id, and the package's shared extractSiteID does not look where this path keeps it. It is called FIRST anyway (reuse before new machinery), then the two extra locations are tried. The extractor is deliberately NOT widened: it has five other callers, several of which treat an empty result as 'skip this work', and silently changing what five unrelated actions resolve is not something a bug patch should do. The extra locations are added here where the blast radius is this action.

bugs_open/092 trap 2: this built page.URL = "/" + page.Name + ".html" when a page had a name but no url -- a hardcoded extension, not NormalizePagePath and not the stored pages.url. On a dir/index.html site or a fleet that does not serve .html that is a confidently wrong address handed to the writer as though it were real, which is the bugs_closed/029 failure mode (an emitter that assembles URLs instead of citing real ones) reintroduced one layer upstream. A url-less page is now dropped and counted. Dropping it is also what lets the database path supply the truth instead of a guess.

092 fix candidate 3, 'fail loudly'. A logger.Warn and an elided prompt section is exactly why this went unnoticed long enough to be measured at 100%: collected_data is pruned at ~24h and pod logs roll, so a day later the fact that a build wrote its links blind is unrecoverable. Writes one agent_error_log row with error_code LINK_CONTEXT_UNAVAILABLE, severity 'error' when no list could be established at all and 'warning' when a fallback saved it. Best-effort by design -- a failure to record must never change the disposition already decided, so it returns nothing and the caller does not branch on it. Direct INSERT rather than orchestration.LogAgentError because that would be an import cycle; same pattern and column list as recordPlanRefusal.
edits.sketch:
INSERT INTO agent_error_log
    (site_id, agent_type, step_name, action, error_message, error_code, severity, context, orchestration_id)
VALUES (NULLIF($1,'')::uuid, $2, $3, 'prepare_link_context', $4, $5, $6, $7::jsonb, NULLIF($8,''))
// error_code = LINK_CONTEXT_UNAVAILABLE; context carries failure/source/page_count/degraded/site_id

edits.rationale: bugs_open/092 trap 1, and the standing landmine in the fleet memory index ('do NOT wire InjectLinkConstraints'). The whole file is a near-duplicate of this action with ZERO call sites anywhere in the tree -- verified per symbol for all five it defines -- and it carries its own copy of the URL synthesis above plus two extra guesses (/blog/ and /tools/ prefixes). Leaving it is how a future thread wires the wrong implementation and the platform ends up with two competing versions of one prompt block. Deleting it retires the landmine rather than restating it. page-content-writer's default_config also carries a dead link_constraints block that no Go code reads; that config is left alone deliberately (config change, separate risk) and is now provably unread.
edits.sketch: git rm platform/orchestration/actions/link_constraints.go  # 173 lines, 5 symbols, 0 external callers

edits.rationale: Nine tests, each pinning a positive artefact rather than 'no error returned' -- the failure mode of this action is producing NOTHING and returning nil, so a test that only checks the error would pass against the bug. Every case was MUTATION-CHECKED on 2026-07-31 against the pre-fix behaviour it guards, and the six mutations are named in the file: restore the empty-string return, drop input_data.site_id from the resolver, restore the URL synthesis, delete the database branch entirely, delete the durable-record call, and reverse the source precedence. All six were caught by exactly the tests that claim to guard them. The collected_data fixture reproduces the SHAPE of a real writer orchestration (input_data.site_id present; db_sync, site_record and top-level site_id absent) because a fixture that helpfully supplied site_record would pass while the live path still resolved nothing.

There is no array of pages anywhere on the run, so repointing pages_field has no valid target and would fail the same silent way. Therefore candidate 1 (have the action query the DB) is the only real option.'

Concept register LNK-017, filed 2026-06-12, status 'partial': 'the writer's prepare_link_context builds an available-pages constraint ... but on the work-item rebuild path no db_sync is mapped, so the constraint text is empty -- the LLM writes prose links unconstrained. Candidate fixes: map db_sync, or make prepare_link_context load pages itself.'

validate_page_content.go:1252 loadValidPagePaths: `SELECT url FROM pages WHERE site_id = $1 AND status NOT IN ('deleted','archived')` -- the predicate this fix copies, so the writer's allow-list equals the gate's accept-set.

Live 2026-07-31, pages table: status distribution is active 449 / archived 23 and NOTHING else; 0 of 472 rows have an empty url; max linkable pages on any one site is 99, mean 30. So the two candidate predicates are the same set today, the url-synthesis path is currently unreachable in production, and the 200-page prompt cap is inert.

Blast radius measured before submitting: exactly one agent_definitions row references prepare_link_context (page-content-writer). All 8 distinct writer runs in the retained window resolve a site id and would gain 31 linkable pages -- 0 -> 31 on every run visible, and the 'no internal links' branch fires on none of them.

bugs_open/092 CORRECTED 2026-07-28: 079's repair 'runs and its output is DISCARDED at persistence ... there is currently no downstream mitigation at all -- the writer invents destinations and they ship.'

Zero call sites: grepped each of the five symbols link_constraints.go defines (InjectLinkConstraints, LinkConstraintsConfig, PageForLinking, extractAvailablePages, convertToPageList) across the whole tree; every hit is inside link_constraints.go itself.
plan.risks: 1) THE VISIBLE CHANGE: every writer prompt on every site now carries an '## Internal Linking' block it has not carried in living memory. That is the point of the fix, but it is a fleet-wide prompt change and content will differ. 2) A site with no pages rows now gets an explicit 'do not create any internal links' instruction. On an initial build where the writer runs before sync_pages_to_db, that could suppress in-prose linking that today happens (unconstrained, and per the evidence essentially always broken -- 15 of 15 unique phantom targets were pure inventions). The collected_data fallback covers the case where a site_plan page list exists. A reviewer should check whether any live workflow writes content before its pages rows exist and would prefer invented links to none. 3) Source precedence is inverted relative to the documented pages_field contract: the database now wins where both exist. Nothing live is lost -- the only producer of db_sync.pages (LoadSiteForRebuildAction) builds it from this same table -- but it is a contract change worth naming. 4) One extra query per writer run (indexed on site_id, LIMIT 201). 5) The deletion of link_constraints.go is safe only because it has zero callers; if a reviewer finds a caller I missed, the delete must come out.
